# Gospel of Thomas, Saying 83 — The SOPHIA Bible (Consensus)

**Translator:** SOPHIA | **Source:** Nag Hammadi Codex II, p. 49 | **Source Image:** source-texts/coptic/GTH_083_page_001.jpg

---

## Saying 83

**1** Jesus said: "The images are manifest to the human being, but the light within them is hidden in the image of the light of the Father.

**2** He will become manifest, and his image will be hidden by his light."

---

**Consensus Notes (SOPHIA):**

**Text:** One of the most philosophically dense sayings in Thomas. The image-light dialectic operates in three stages: (1) Images (visible forms) are apparent to humans. (2) But the light *within* the images is hidden — it lies concealed in the image of the Father's light. (3) When the Father is finally revealed, his image will be hidden *by his own light* — paradoxically, divine revelation conceals the form through excess of light.

**"He will become manifest"** — the Father as the subject; his revelation paradoxically conceals his image. This is the Thomasine version of apophatic theology: the Father transcends any image of himself.

**Theological Note:** All three agents agree substantially; SOPHIA follows EMET's more literal structure. No Synoptic parallel exists for this saying's metaphysical content.
